The route for remove_member is delete "members" in config/routes.rb, but this spec issues xhr :put. Controller specs do not check the HTTP verb against the routes, so the test passes regardless of which verb is mapped. It should use :delete so it exercises the real endpoint.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the remove_member spec issues xhr :put, but the route maps remove_member to DELETE and the spec should use :delete.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit

totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With 100 members and limit 50 this yields 3 pages, not 2. Page 2 shows Next as enabled, and clicking it requests offset 100, which returns an empty page labelled 3/3. Math.ceil(user_count / limit) gives the correct count for all values.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same off-by-one totalPages bug from Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 when the count is an exact multiple of limit, using the 100/50 example and the empty extra page.

false_positives.candidate:
Public member list silently capped at 50 with no paging UI

The members action now applies a default limit of 50 to every group. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. The public members route (group-members.js.es6) calls findMembers() once with the defaults, and the template group/members.hbs has no next/previous controls. In any group with more than 50 members, the public page shows only the first 50 and gives users no way to reach the rest. Either add paging to the public page or keep returning the full list there.

GET /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed from array to object

The endpoint used to return a bare JSON array of serialized members. It now returns {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}. Any existing consumer that treats the response as an array (API clients, plugins, other frontend code) will break. The change is not versioned or called out, and only the consumers in this PR were updated.

Negative limit or offset causes a database error (500)

limit and offset come straight from params through to_i with no validation. A negative value (for example offset=-1) is passed into LIMIT/OFFSET, which PostgreSQL rejects, so the request returns a 500 instead of a client error. Previously only automatic groups reached this code path with user-supplied limit/offset; now every group's member endpoint does.

create ignores alias_level, which the admin UI sends for new groups

The admin form shows the alias_level combo box for new groups too, and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on POST. create only reads name and visible, so the chosen alias level is silently dropped and the group is created with the default. The save action does not call save() again after create, so the value is never persisted. The spec suite has no create test that checks alias_level.

PATCH incremental membership API removed; PATCH now silently succeeds without changes

The old update_patch handled PATCH with a changes payload (add/delete usernames). That branch is removed, but resources :groups still routes PATCH to update. update now ignores the changes key, saves name/visible/alias_level, and returns success. Existing API clients get HTTP 200 and no membership change, which is a silent no-op instead of an error. Either keep the behaviour or reject PATCH explicitly.

Removing a non-member raises RecordNotFound instead of succeeding

group.users.delete(user_id) is called with an integer id. In Rails 4.x, CollectionProxy#delete with ids first calls find on the association, so a user who is not in the group raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound and returns a 404. The removed spec explicitly tested that removing non-members succeeds silently, and the admin JS removeMember has no error handler, so a stale list just fails with no feedback.

Behaviour changes are untested: pagination endpoint, unknown usernames, non-members, alias_level on create

The PR changes the public members endpoint (paginated, new response shape) but adds no test for it in the groups controller spec. It also removes the specs for adding unknown users and removing non-members without replacing them. There is no create test covering alias_level, which is why the dropped value above goes unnoticed. The JS pagination arithmetic (totalPages) has no test either.

Remove control shown for automatic groups because the template checks the wrong object

This template is rendered once per member, so its context is the member User object. {{#unless automatic}} therefore looks up automatic on the user, which is undefined, and the remove link renders for every member, including automatic groups. Clicking it sends a DELETE that the server rejects with a 422, and the UI has no error handler, so nothing visible happens. The flag should be passed in from the group controller.

Selector for the old user-selector id no longer matches

The user-selector input was renamed from id group-users to user-selector in group.hbs, but this rule still targets input#group-users, so its width no longer applies. The enclosing .row.groups rule is also unused now. The selector should be updated or removed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation has a side effect that inflates match_count on every valid? call

`BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` increments `match_count` and saves the record each time it runs. It runs on every validation of a changed email. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save` (line 172), which validates again, so one blocked signup attempt is counted twice. The statistic is wrong, and any other `valid?` call also inflates it. Record matches in an explicit step outside the validator, and keep the validator read-only.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a write (incrementing match_count and saving) during what should be a read/validation check. The candidate adds a concrete double-counting consequence, but the underlying side-effect concern matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Whitelist regex is unanchored, so suffix-extended domains pass the whitelist

The whitelist check builds `/@(gmail\.com)/i` with no end anchor. An address such as `attacker@gmail.com.evil.example` matches and passes a `gmail.com` whitelist. The code was carried over from `User#email_in_restriction_setting?`, but it now lives in a new validator and the whitelist is an access-control policy. Anchor the domain (for example `/@(domain)$/i` after escaping) and compare the domain part exactly. The domain strings are also interpolated into the regex without `Regexp.escape`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the whitelist regex lacks proper anchoring, so it matches domain suffixes/extensions rather than exact domains. The candidate's example differs in direction but describes the same boundary-anchoring failure.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so a case variant of a blocked address gets through

`should_block?` looks up `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` using the raw value. Nothing normalizes the address before the lookup: `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` as typed and `User` has no downcasing callback. An entry for `spammer@spamclub.com` therefore does not match a signup with `Spammer@SpamClub.com`, and the spammer can register anyway. The existing domain restrictions in the same validator use a case-insensitive regex, so they are not affected. The uniqueness validation on `BlockedEmail#email` is also case-sensitive, so case-variant duplicate entries can be created. Normalize with `Email.downcase` on both the stored value and the lookup input, or match case-insensitively.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a case-sensitive email lookup, so a case variant of a blocked address can bypass the block. The candidate adds normalization details but describes the same underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
match_count is a non-atomic read-modify-write that loses concurrent increments

`record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` reads the count, adds one in Ruby, and writes it back. Two concurrent signups matching the same entry can both write the same value, so the count is undercounted. The full `save` also re-runs validations, including a uniqueness query, for what is a counter bump. Use an atomic database update such as `BlockedEmail.update_counters` or `update_all` with `match_count = match_count + 1`.

Client caches server email rejections for the session and never re-checks them

Any server error on `email` pushes the address into `rejectedEmails`, which is a controller-lifetime array. Later the client treats that address as invalid without asking the server. If an admin later removes the block or changes the whitelist, the user is still blocked in the browser until a reload. The client also overrides the server's specific message with the generic `user.email.invalid` text. The server should stay the only authority on blocked addresses, so keep the rejection only for the current form submission or drop the client-side check.

Specs stub out the blocklist lookup, so the real behavior is untested

Both examples stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so the tests never touch the database or the normalization path. Nothing covers case variants of a blocked address, which is the bypass above. Nothing checks that a blocked signup through `User`/`UsersController` is rejected, or that a single attempt increments `match_count` only once, which is the double-count above. The uniqueness and case behavior of `BlockedEmail` are also untested. Add an integration-level spec that creates a blocked entry, attempts signup with a case-variant address, and asserts the rejection and the count.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`align-items` mixin emits a bogus `-ms-align-items` property

`-ms-align-items` is not a real CSS property. The correct IE10 prefixed property is `-ms-flex-align`, which the same mixin already emits on line 120. The line is dead and misleading: it suggests IE support is covered by a property name that browsers never recognise. It should be removed.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: `-ms-align-items` is not a valid legacy property, and the correct IE/Edge prefix is `-ms-flex-align`.

false_positives.candidate:
Floated button inside the new flex container loses its right alignment

`.small-action` is converted to `display: flex` in this PR, but the `button` rule inside it still relies on `float: right`. Floats are ignored on flex items, so if the button is a direct child of `.small-action`, it stops being pushed to the right edge and sits right after `.small-action-desc`. `.small-action-desc` has no `flex-grow`, so nothing fills the remaining space to keep the button at the end. The button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the float should be removed and the placement set through flex properties). Otherwise the action button in small-action posts visibly moves.

`order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` has no effect unless its parent is a flex container

`order` only applies to flex or box items. This PR does not make the parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` (`#topic-title`) a flex container, and no changed file does. Unless another stylesheet establishes flex layout there, the `@include order(2)` is a no-op. The same change also adds `line-height: 1.5`, which is unrelated to ordering. The author should confirm the flex parent exists or drop the ordering.

Bullet badge top margin inside `.extra-info-wrapper` removed without replacement

The `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` is deleted, and nothing replaces it. Bullet badges in the topic title lose their 5px top offset, which changes their vertical alignment. The PR does not mention this and the title only refers to performance, so it looks like an unintended visual regression.

PR description is a placeholder and does not explain the many visual changes

The description reads only "Test 5", and the title claims a performance optimization. The diff is a layout refactor from floats to flexbox across header, topic title, post, small-action and badge styles. It also changes spacing: `.small-action-desc` loses its vertical padding and 4em left padding, `margin-top` is removed, and `.title` and `.panel` float rules are replaced. None of this is justified, and no performance measurement is offered. Reviewers cannot tell which changes are intentional or how they were verified, so the description should explain the intent and the visual impact.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the '?' and is never called

The serializer's include hooks follow the `include_<attr>?` convention (see `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_suspend_reason?`). This method is named `include_website_name` with no question mark, so ActiveModel Serializer will not find it when deciding whether to emit the attribute. The intended `website.present?` condition therefore never runs, and `website_name` is emitted as `null` for every user with no website. Renaming it to `include_website_name?` would fix the contract, though the leak above still needs the untrusted gating.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same core bug: include_website_name lacks the required ? suffix, so the serializer never invokes the conditional inclusion hook. It omits the secondary string-concatenation concern, but the primary issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name bypasses the TL0 restriction and exposes a hidden website to anonymous viewers

`website` is gated by `untrusted_attributes`, so for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous or restricted scope it is omitted. The new `website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list (line 43), not to `untrusted_attributes`, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` without calling `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The result is that the website's domain (and now its path, via the new same-domain branch) is still serialized and rendered by user.hbs line 66 for restricted users. This defeats the intentional hiding of TL0 website data. Adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (around line 105) would apply the existing gate, and the custom `include_` method would be unnecessary.

Domain comparison is case-sensitive, so mixed-case website hosts lose the path

`URI(...).host` preserves the case typed by the user, but `Discourse.current_hostname` is compared with `==` here and with `ends_with?` and `split` below. A website such as `http://Example.com/user` on an instance at `example.com` does not match the first branch, falls through to the parent-domain check, and returns just `Example.com` with the path dropped. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so the host should be downcased before comparing.

Homepage URLs with a trailing slash render as 'example.com/'

For a website like `https://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` returns `"/"`, so the first branch returns `"example.com/"`. This is a very common way to enter a homepage and produces an awkward trailing slash in the profile. The path should be ignored when it is empty or `"/"`.

Untrusted attribute list was not updated for the new website_name attribute

The TL0-anonymous spec asserts that `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background` are not serialized, but it does not include `website_name`. Because `website_name` is ungated, this spec gives false confidence: it would still pass while the domain leaks for restricted users. Adding `website_name` here and setting a website on the TL0 fixture would catch the regression.

Missing coverage for the www/forum sibling-subdomain branch and for a blank website

The `website_name` examples cover the exact-match branch and the parent-domain branch, but not the middle branch in the serializer (same label count, same parent domain, e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forums.example.com`). That branch has its own path-appending logic and is untested. There is also no example for a user with no website, which is where `website_name` should return nil and the attribute should be omitted (the `include_` logic that is currently broken).

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Kernel#open used on an unvalidated admin-set URL

`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` calls Kernel#open. feed_polling_url has no URL validation. On Ruby versions before 3.0, a value beginning with `|` is run as a shell command, and an arbitrary path is read as a local file. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (or validate the scheme first) so only http(s) is fetched.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same unvalidated open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) call. The candidate's command/file-read details are additional consequences of that issue, while its HTTP(S) restriction recommendation addresses the golden comment's arbitrary URL fetch concern.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Origin check is a substring match, not an origin comparison

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` passes whenever e.origin is a textual prefix of the forum URL. For discourseUrl `https://forum.example.com/`, an origin of `https://forum.example.co` passes. A page on such a domain can post discourse-resize messages and control the iframe height. Compare e.origin for equality with the origin parsed from discourseUrl.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same origin-validation bypass: indexOf performs a substring/prefix check rather than comparing origins, allowing the message to be mishandled. The candidate gives a different example but describes the same bug and fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
X-Frame-Options value ALLOWALL is not a defined value

The only defined X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and ALLOW-FROM. Browsers ignore ALLOWALL, so this header has no effect whatever the comment or the intent suggests. If framing from any origin is intended, remove the header and use CSP frame-ancestors. If the goal is to override a stricter app-wide default, this does not do that either.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same core defect: setting X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL is invalid and provides no clickjacking protection. The candidate explains browsers ignore the undefined value and suggests CSP frame-ancestors, which aligns with the golden comment's concern even though it omits the referer-bypass details.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Unescaped embed URL interpolated into stored raw HTML footer enables stored XSS The footer is built as `#{url}` with the URL unescaped, and the result is saved as a raw_html post. `Post#cook` returns raw for raw_html posts and nothing sanitizes it, so any quote in the URL breaks out of the attribute. The URL reaches this code from the `embed_url` query parameter of `/embed/best` via TopicRetriever, which only checks the host. A URL such as `http:///?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` passes URI parsing (apostrophes and `=` are legal in the query), and the remote returns 200 for any existing path. An anonymous visitor can therefore plant an event handler in a topic that every reader, including forum users on the Discourse origin, will execute. Escape the URL (e.g. CGI.escapeHTML / ERB::Util.html_escape) in both the attribute and the text, or build the link with Nokogiri.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment flags two problems in TopicEmbed.import, including an XSS vulnerability from unescaped URL interpolation in generated HTML. The candidate identifies that same XSS issue in detail (unescaped embed URL in raw HTML footer), even though it does not mention the separate NoMethodError.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Stray `end if` in template is malformed and breaks the embed view

`<%- end if %>` closes the if/else but then starts a modifier `if` that applies to the next emitted output statement. Depending on how the ERB handler terminates the statement, this either fails to compile (every /embed/best render then errors) or reorders the output so the logo link is evaluated as a condition. The intended terminator is `<%- end %>`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same malformed ERB terminator, noting that `<%- end if %>` should be `<%- end %>` to properly close the if block.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
A feed item without content aborts the whole poll; String#scrub needs Ruby 2.1+

`i.content` is nil when an RSS item has no content element, so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The loop stops, so the remaining items are never imported. PollFeed sets `retry: false`, so the hourly job just fails until the feed changes. TopicRetriever calls the same code, so one bad item also fails an unrelated visitor's retrieval. In addition, String#scrub only exists on Ruby 2.1+, so on older Rubies this line fails for every item. Guard nil content (and nil title) and skip or fall back per item.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: calling scrub on i.content assumes content is present, but RSS items can lack content, causing a nil-related crash. The candidate adds extra context but points to the same underlying issue and fallback/guard fix.

false_positives.candidate:
raw_html cook method permanently disables sanitization for every later edit

`cook` returns the raw string whenever cook_method is raw_html, and before_save re-cooks on every update. Nothing resets cook_method, so any edit to an imported post, by any editor, is stored as cooked HTML with no PrettyText sanitization and with the `after_post_cook` plugin filters skipped. The flag was meant for trusted feed/readability imports but is not scoped to the import path. Restrict raw_html to creation by the importer, or re-cook through PrettyText on updates.

Retrieval throttle keyed on the full URL can be bypassed to amplify remote fetches

The 60-second throttle key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, which includes the query string. Anonymous visitors can vary the query on each request and get a fresh key every time, so each request triggers an outbound fetch of the embeddable host. With feed polling enabled, each job also runs a full RSS poll and re-imports every feed item. EmbedController enqueues `retrieve_topic` for any embed_url before the host is validated (embed_controller.rb line 15), so garbage URLs also create jobs. Validate the host in the controller before enqueueing, and throttle per host or per normalized URL.

Post-commit jobs and publishes run inside the outer Topic.transaction

TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator.create in Topic.transaction. PostCreator#create calls enqueue_jobs (process_post, feature_topic_users) and publishes to MessageBus and TopicTrackingState before the outer transaction commits. PostCreator's own comment says jobs must be enqueued after commit. A Sidekiq worker can therefore run process_post before the post is visible. Separately, the check-then-create (`TopicEmbed.where(...).first` then `create!`) races with a concurrent import of the same URL (feed poll vs. retrieve_topic). The unique index blocks the duplicate row, but the RecordNotUnique error is unhandled and the rolled-back topic has already been announced. Move the import outside the enclosing transaction or defer enqueues with after_commit, and rescue the unique violation.

Scheme check uses ^ which matches at any line start

`url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` passes if any line of the string starts with http(s)://, so `"javascript:alert(1)\nhttp://x"` is accepted. The value is then written into the footer href and stored as embed_url. Use `\A` (and the same change in PollFeed's `url !~` check, poll_feed.rb line 33).

Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten into broken same-site paths

`href.start_with?('/')` is true for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`. The `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes, producing `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`. The same applies to img src (line 71). The comment says relative URLs are converted, but only root-relative paths are handled. Protocol-relative URLs should get only the scheme prefixed.

Remote fetch has no timeout and reads the whole body into memory

`open(url).read` uses open-uri defaults with no open or read timeout and no size cap. A slow or hanging embeddable host blocks the Sidekiq worker indefinitely, and a very large response is loaded entirely into memory. Set open_timeout and read_timeout and limit the body size.

'is 404 without an embed_url' does not test the missing parameter

embeddable_host defaults to '', so the before_filter ensure_embeddable raises InvalidAccess before `params.require(:embed_url)` runs. The example passes because of the host check, not the missing parameter, and its name is wrong (the response is a 403-style access error, not 404). Stub a valid host and referer, then call `get :best` without embed_url to test what the name claims.

create_table with force: true drops an existing topic_embeds table

If topic_embeds already exists when this migration runs (partly migrated database, or a table created by an earlier revision of this branch), `force: true` drops it along with every embed-to-topic mapping. Once the mappings are gone, the next retrieval of each embedded article creates a duplicate topic. Remove `force: true`.

Existing migration changed to force-drop top_topics

This edits an already-merged migration to add `force: true`. For any database where top_topics exists when the migration runs, the table and its counters are dropped and then rebuilt. Migrations should not drop tables. Revert to the original, or guard with `table_exists?`.

NOT NULL column with default rewrites the posts table

On PostgreSQL before 11, `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` rewrites the whole posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking reads and writes for the duration on a large forum. Add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then add the default and NOT NULL constraint.

Disqus importer silently changes behaviour and drops --category

This change is outside the stated embed scope and is not documented. The `--category` option is removed, so `-c` no longer works. The first post's created_at is no longer set. Each thread is now fetched live via TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of an offline import, so an unreachable page, a 404, or a nil t[:link] (open(nil) raises TypeError) now breaks or skips the import. Split this into its own change with a documented migration path.

embed_url is varchar(255) with no length guard; longer URLs fail at insert

`t.string :embed_url` becomes varchar(255) on PostgreSQL. The URL comes straight from the request query string, and TopicRetriever and TopicEmbed only check the host and presence. A URL over 255 characters makes TopicEmbed.create! raise StatementInvalid after the topic and post were created inside the transaction. The job fails, and the embed page keeps showing 'Loading' and re-enqueuing. Validate length in the model or the controller, or use a text column.

cook_method option honoured with no permission check

Setting cook_method to raw_html disables PrettyText sanitization for the post. Nothing in this diff restricts who may set it. If any controller passes request params or a user-supplied hash into PostCreator, any user can store unsanitized HTML. Confirm callers only pass server-chosen values, or restrict this option to the import path.

setnx followed by expire is not atomic; a crash leaves a permanent throttle key

If the process dies or expire fails between `setnx` and `expire`, the key has no TTL. retrieved_recently? then returns true forever for that URL, so the embed can never be retrieved again without manual Redis cleanup. Use a single atomic SET with NX and EX options.

Missing embed_by_username silently skips import, leaving visitors on a loading page

If embed_by_username is unset or names no user, fetch_http returns without logging or raising. The embedding visitor sees 'Loading Discussion...' and the page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no error for the admin. Validate the setting, or log the failure.

poll_feed itself is untested; spec only covers the execute gating

All examples only check whether execute delegates to poll_feed. Feed parsing, item-to-topic import, and the URL fallback are not exercised, which is why the nil-content crash in poll_feed.rb goes unnoticed. The file also requires an unrelated job (jobs/regular/process_post).

A slot that starts inside the working window and runs past its end is not rejected here. The variable should use slotEndTime.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: comparing dayjs objects with === checks references and always returns false, preventing the intended zero-length check. The candidate correctly recommends isSame or explicit handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check entirely

When a slot falls inside a same-day date override, none of the early-return branches in the find callback fire, so find returns undefined but dateOverrideExist is already true. The following `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` then returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at the end of the function. Calendar events and existing bookings overlapping the slot are therefore ignored for any host (fixed or round-robin) who has a date override on that day. A round-robin host with a conflict inside their override window stays eligible and can be double-booked. Overrides should narrow availability, not bypass conflict checks; this branch should fall through to the busy check instead of returning true. No test covers a busy time inside an override.

Days with more than one date override row reject every slot

dateOverrides.find returns the first override for which the callback returns truthy, and the callback returns true whenever the slot is outside that particular override (lines 118-124). With two override rows on the same day, for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00 (the UI stores each range as its own row), a 09:00 slot is inside the first but the second callback returns true, so find returns it and line 130 returns false. The same happens for a 14:00 slot. Every slot on that day is rejected even though slots in both windows are valid. The intended logic is 'available if inside any override on that day', which needs some() with the correct polarity, not find with inverted returns.

Split working hours on one weekday remove all slots for that day

workingHours.find returns the first entry on the slot's weekday whose range does not contain the slot (the callback returns true when start < startTime or end > endTime). If a host has two ranges on the same weekday, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 (a lunch break, stored as two availability rows), a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the 13:00-17:00 entry, and a 14:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the 09:00-12:00 entry. The host gets no slots on that day. getSlots already restricts slots to working hours, so this block is either redundant or, as written, breaks split schedules. The existing tests only use one contiguous range per day, so this is not caught.

Fixed host's days off are not enforced for round-robin slots

The working-hours check only rejects a slot when an entry for the same weekday exists and does not contain it. If a fixed host has no working-hours entry for the slot's weekday (for example a Monday-Friday host and a Saturday slot), find returns undefined and nothing rejects the slot. The slot is generated from the round-robin host's hours, and the fixed host's check then only looks at busy times, so the slot passes. A round-robin event with a fixed host who does not work Saturdays still offers and books Saturday slots with that fixed host. This is the exact problem the PR says it fixes. A fixed host should be treated as unavailable when the slot is not on one of their working days.

Shifted override minutes wrap past midnight and land on the wrong day

startTime and endTime take only .hour()*60 + .minute() of the offset-shifted instant, which drops the date. The day an override is assigned to comes from the unshifted override.start in the activeOverrides filter, so when the offset pushes the time across midnight the result is attributed to the wrong day. Example: organizer America/New_York, invitee Europe/London, override starting 23:00 UTC on day D. The filter assigns it to London day D. offset = 0 - (-300) = +300, so the shifted time is 04:00 on day D+1, but the code yields 240 and shows 04:00 on day D. Day D+1 loses the override entirely. Evening overrides viewed from zones ahead of the organizer will be misplaced like this. The shifted timestamp should be kept as a full datetime and the day derived from it, not reduced to minutes-of-day.

Override day match mixes server-local and UTC formatting

dayjs(date.start).add(...).format(...) is in local mode, so it formats in the process timezone, while slotStartTime.format(...) is in UTC (time.utc()). The two strings are compared to decide whether an override applies to the slot's day. On any process not running in UTC, near midnight an override can be matched to the wrong day or not matched at all, which then sends the slot to the working-hours check instead. Both sides should be formatted in UTC.

Optional override timeZone is passed to tz() with no fallback

TimeRange.timeZone was just made optional, but getSlots passes override.timeZone straight into .tz() without a fallback, even though organizerTimeZone is already in scope in this function. When timeZone is undefined, dayjs falls back to the default or the process local zone, so the organizer offset is computed against the wrong zone without any error. The fallback should be organizerTimeZone, or the code should fail loudly.

toHaveTimeSlots passes when fewer slots than expected are returned

The matcher iterates over the actual slots only (.every over schedule.slots[date]) and compares each to expectedSlots[index]. Missing trailing expected slots are never detected, so an assertion expecting four override slots passes if only one matching slot is returned. Every new override assertion depends on this matcher, so regressions that remove slots (multiple override rows on one day, fixed host days off, split working hours) would go unnoticed. The matcher should also assert the lengths match.

Headline scenarios of the PR have no test coverage

The PR's main change, fixed-host date overrides in round-robin events, has no test. The only new test is an extra assertion in the single-host override test, which has no hosts, no busy times, and one override row. None of the regressions in this change are exercised: a busy time inside an override, two override rows on the same day, a split working-hours day, or a fixed host without working hours on the slot's weekday. Tests should cover each of these, and the round-robin plus fixed-host override case the PR describes.

New timeZone field on TimeRange is undocumented and its semantics are load-bearing

The new optional timeZone is added without a comment. The code relies on an undocumented convention: override start and end are treated as organizer wall-clock time carried in their UTC fields, and the organizer's offset is applied in both lib/slots.ts and checkIfIsAvailable. Nothing in this type says which timezone the field refers to or how start and end should be interpreted, so a future change to getUserAvailability could break the override logic silently.

Reminders then get more attempts than intended before the give-up delete triggers. Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` avoids this. The same pattern is repeated at line 195.

The success-path updates at lines 169 and 179 can throw into this same catch, so the risk is not limited to the new code path.

The schema has no index on retryCount, and Postgres cannot use the existing (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index for an OR when one branch is unindexed, so every cron invocation scans the whole WorkflowReminder table. That table grows with every booking step, and this runs on a frequent cron. Either add an index on retryCount or issue the two conditions as separate deletes.

Reminders with no message or no sendTo are never counted as failures

If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing, neither the success branch nor the new else/catch increments retryCount runs. Those reminders stay unscheduled and are re-fetched and skipped on every cron run until scheduledDate passes, never reaching the give-up threshold. The `continue` at lines 68-70 for a missing workflowStep or booking has the same effect. This is a failure to send that the PR's retry-then-delete logic is meant to cover but does not.

No tests for the retry and give-up behavior

The PR changes the cron's retry semantics (increment on failure, increment on catch, delete when retryCount > 1) but adds no test. Nothing verifies that a failed Twilio schedule increments the counter, that a second failure leads to deletion on the next run, or that the catch path behaves correctly. The regression described in the catch-block finding would also go unnoticed without a test.

Generated kysely and zod artifacts were not regenerated (if committed)

The schema declares generators for prisma-kysely (output `../kysely`) and zod-prisma (output `./zod`). Adding a column to WorkflowReminder normally requires regenerating those artifacts. The PR does not touch them. If they are checked into the repo, their WorkflowReminder types will lack retryCount and will drift from the database. Please confirm whether these are committed and regenerate them if so.

The diff deletes the public `findMany` method, which executed the query and returned rows, and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment. `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` also change their return type from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`. Callers must now write their own `$queryRaw` and embed the fragment. The PR description frames the change as a test-only update and never mentions removing the public method or changing these return types.

The entire `describe("Caching")` block, with the tests 'should cache authorization conditions' and 'should cache filter conditions', was removed. The service still memoizes results in `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so the repeat-call behaviour these tests covered now has no test. The PR description does not mention removing them.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code login skips the password check when any totpCode is sent

The password check is gated on `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. Any non-empty totpCode makes the whole password verification block get skipped. The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs regardless of the password, so a request with the email, a valid backup code, and any non-empty totpCode logs in without a password. The login UI clears totpCode in backup mode, so normal use is unaffected, but the credentials callback is reachable directly. The consequence is that a backup code, which is meant to be a second factor, becomes a standalone login credential. A leaked backup-codes download is enough to take over the account. The same gate already lets email plus a valid TOTP skip the password, and this PR extends that bypass to the new code path. The password must be verified independently of which second factor is used.

Backup codes are unreachable on the external TOTP screen (IdP/redirect login)

The 'Lost access' button exists only in TwoFactorFooter. When totpEmail is set, which the signIn callbacks produce via loginWithTotp for accounts with 2FA, footerText uses ExternalTotpFooter, which offers only Cancel. The BackupCode screen therefore cannot be reached for those users, so the backup codes feature does not work for them. Even if the button were added, the identityProvider guard in next-auth-options.ts (line 113) rejects non-CAL accounts when totpCode is empty, so the backend would also need changing. The feature should either be offered on that screen with the backend path fixed, or the gap should be documented.

Dismissing the dialog on the backup codes step permanently loses the codes

The Dialog's onOpenChange is passed straight through (line 166). On the DisplayBackupCodes step, Escape, an outside click, or the close icon dismisses the dialog with no warning, and onEnable is not called. By this point the enable endpoint has already succeeded, so 2FA is active on the server. The codes are stored only encrypted, and no endpoint returns them again, so the user ends up with 2FA on, no copy of the codes, and the parent never notified. Their only way out is to disable 2FA. Guard onOpenChange on this step, or treat dismissal like the Close button, and tell the user on this screen that the codes will be shown only once.

missing_backup_codes tells users to generate codes in settings, which is not possible

The message reads 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' Nothing in this PR provides a settings UI or endpoint to generate backup codes. They are created only during the 2FA setup flow, and disabling 2FA clears them. Users who enabled 2FA before this change, or whose codes were cleared, are sent to do something that cannot be done. The text should describe a real recovery path, or regeneration should be added.

Unrelated tabIndex=-1 on the shared PasswordField visibility toggle

The show/hide password button now has tabIndex={-1}. PasswordField is shared by every password input in the app (login, signup, password change), not only the 2FA flow, and this change is unrelated to backup codes. It removes the toggle from keyboard tab order, so keyboard-only users can no longer reveal a password they are typing. Either drop the change or justify and scope it separately.

The new backup-code login path has no test coverage

The PR's own test plan step 2 (log in via 'Lost access' with a backup code) has no e2e or unit test. The TODO on this line acknowledges the gap. The authorize backup branch in next-auth-options.ts and the backup branch in disable.ts are also untested, which is how the password-gate bypass above went unnoticed. At minimum the tests should cover: a backup code logs in once, a second use is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode, a wrong code is rejected, and a backup code without the password fails.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unguarded property access crashes create() for Meet bookings without a destination calendar

`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined`, but the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. handleNewBooking now passes `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, so `evt.destinationCalendar` becomes `[]`. For a booking with Google Meet location, this throws a TypeError inside create() and the booking fails. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same null-reference bug: destructuring evt.destinationCalendar when it is null/empty yields undefined, and then accessing a property on mainHostDestinationCalendar crashes. The candidate focuses on create() and the integration access, while the golden also mentions updateEvent(), but the underlying issue is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent resolves calendarId to undefined when externalCalendarId is empty; deleteEvent falls back to primary

The new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then compares `cal.externalId` against that falsy value, so it matches nothing and returns undefined. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. As a result calendarId is undefined and the Google update fails for booking references that have no externalCalendarId. The same bug is at line 317 in deleteEvent: the lookup returns undefined, so deletion silently targets 'primary' and the event remains on the calendar the user actually picked. Fix: select the destination calendar by credential or take the first destination instead of comparing against externalCalendarId.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same faulty destination-calendar lookup: comparing cal.externalId to externalCalendarId cannot find the intended calendar, leaving calendarId undefined. The candidate adds the deleteEvent fallback consequence but points to the same underlying logic bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug and requestedSlug conditions are inverted

The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})` (line 153). This flips the logic. With billing disabled (self-hosted), the org is created with no slug. With billing enabled, the slug is written immediately and the requestedSlug approval flow is bypassed. This change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and is not mentioned in the description.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same inverted conditional logic around organization creation: slug and requestedSlug are now both applied when team billing is enabled and neither when disabled, reversing the intended behavior.

false_positives.candidate:
Video references are saved without credentialId, so cancelled video meetings are never deleted

The previous code set `credentialId` to `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results. The new code sets it to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so every video reference is written with credentialId undefined. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is truthy (`if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`). Cancelled bookings will therefore leave the video meeting (Zoom, Daily, Meet, etc.) alive.

Office365 and Lark createEvent use the organizer's destination calendar for every credential

createEvent takes `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar` and builds the URL from its externalId, ignoring which credential is calling. For collective events, the team member's O365 credential is therefore asked to write to the organizer's calendar id. Graph returns 404 and the member's event is never created. The Lark createEvent (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 128) has the same flaw. The Google implementation avoids this by matching on credentialId. The stated goal, that every host with any calendar app receives the event, is not met for these providers.

CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for team hosts whose calendars don't match the organizer's destination

The filter `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` uses the first destination calendar, which belongs to the organizer, even when the call is made with a team member's credential. The team member's CalDAV account has no calendar with that URL, so the filter returns an empty list. responses is then empty, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and createEvent returns a success result with a uid. The member gets no event and no error is surfaced.

Destination calendars without credentialId lose their externalId, so events land in primary

In the else branch the destination's externalId is dropped: `createEvent(c, event)` is called without it. Google's createEvent resolves the calendar only by matching a destination with the credential's id, so for a legacy destination calendar with no credentialId the event goes to 'primary' instead of the calendar the user selected. The reference then stores externalCalendarId as undefined. The previous code used destinationCalendar.externalId for both the insert and the stored reference.

Hangout-link patch uses an undefined calendarId and its promise is neither awaited nor caught

The insert falls back to 'primary' (`selectedCalendar || "primary"`), but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When no destination calendar matches the credential, which is common when a user has no destination row, selectedCalendar is undefined. The patch is built with an undefined calendar and is fire-and-forget, so the description never gets the Meet link and the rejection is unhandled. Fix: reuse the same resolved calendar id as the insert.

Recurring-cancel deletion runs once per calendar reference, causing duplicate deletes

The loop now iterates over every calendar reference, but the recurring branch builds `promises` from the full updatedBookings list and the user's calendar credentials. That block does not depend on the current reference, so with N references every updated booking's event is deleted N times on every calendar. This wastes external API calls and can trigger rate limits. The recurring deletion should run once outside the per-reference loop.

Team hosts' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none

evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The collective-host calendars are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which is a silent no-op on null. In that case no host other than the organizer receives the event, even though their calendars are connected. Build the array explicitly (`[...(base ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`) instead of pushing onto a possibly-null value.

Webhook payload destinationCalendar changes from object to array without notice

The field is part of the webhook payload (see the e2e expectations in apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts). Subscribers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or similar will break. Empty values are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking emits null, while confirm, cancel, and reschedule emit []. For collective events the payload now also includes every host's DestinationCalendar row, with userId, credentialId, and externalId (often the account email for Google). This is a breaking, undocumented API change that also widens the data sent to subscribers.

Collective and multi-calendar behaviour changed without tests

The PR checklist states no tests were added, yet this change reworks destination-calendar routing across EventManager, the Google/Lark/Office365/CalDAV services, and booking cancel/reschedule. The regressions noted in this review (null-safety on the Meet branch, video credentialId, legacy destination routing, updateLocation references) are the kind of thing unit tests of EventManager would catch. At minimum, existing EventManager tests need to be updated for the array shape.

loadUsers error handling leaks Prisma error messages as 400s and masks other failures as 500s

The catch block turns any Prisma known-request error into an HttpError 400 using `error.message`, so raw database error text goes to the API client. Any other error, such as a thrown Error from the empty-dynamicUserList check, becomes a generic 500 'Unable to load users', which discards the real cause. Database failures should be a 500 with a generic message, and validation errors should keep their specific messages.

updateLocation writes calendar references without credentialId or externalCalendarId

CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return credentialId or externalId in its EventResult. The new `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` and `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` therefore store null for calendar references. The previous code fell back to evt.destinationCalendar. Those references are then used by handleCancelBooking, which takes the legacy path and deletes by uid on every calendar of that type, or targets 'primary' for Google, so the real event is left behind.

Reschedule with newBookingId deletes only the first old calendar event

After updating calendar events for all references, the merge path still picks a single old calendar reference with `booking.references.find(...)`. Bookings with several calendar references (the collective multi-host case this PR enables) keep the old events on the other hosts' calendars.

Confirming a collective booking never includes team hosts' destination calendars

The confirm handler builds evt.destinationCalendar only from the booking's destination or the organizer's. Unlike handleNewBooking, it does not add collective hosts' calendars. Bookings that require confirmation are therefore created only on the organizer's calendar when confirmed. The same gap exists in the Stripe and PayPal payment-success paths, which also build evt from the booking and organizer only.

Dynamic-user query drops the organization select without explanation

The findMany for dynamic users previously selected `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. That select is removed here with no replacement. Any downstream code that reads users[].organization will get undefined. The change is unrelated to the PR's purpose and should be justified or reverted.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
forEach(async) detaches calendar/video cancellation and disables the try/catch

The callback passed to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is now async and awaits getCalendar, but Array.prototype.forEach ignores the returned promise. Consequences: (1) the try/catch at lines 124-139 can no longer catch anything. getCalendar, deleteEvent and deleteMeeting failures become unhandled promise rejections, which crash Node by default on v15+. (2) Reschedule returns true before the calendar and video cancellations have run, so the booking is marked cancelled while the old calendar slot may still be held. Fix by using a for...of loop with await inside the existing try block.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: an async callback passed to forEach is not awaited, so calendar/video cancellation promises escape the surrounding try/catch and the function returns before cleanup completes. Its recommended for...of fix also matches the golden comment.

false_positives.candidate:
forEach(async) detaches calendar/video cancellation and disables the try/catch

Same defect as the vital reschedule: the forEach callback is async and awaits getCalendar, but forEach does not await it. The surrounding try/catch no longer sees errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting, which become unhandled rejections. The function also returns true before the cancellations finish. Use for...of with await so the existing try/catch and ordering actually apply.

Unawaited async forEach in requestReschedule drops errors and races the response

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach now takes an async callback that awaits getCalendar and then calls deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. forEach does not await these promises, and this block has no try/catch. The mutation proceeds to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and returns while calendar and video deletions are still in flight. Any rejection (credential failure, network error) becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of a handled error. Replace with for...of and await each deletion, or collect the promises and Promise.allSettled them.

Calendar deletions in an unawaited forEach(async) are never awaited and their errors are lost

The recurring-cancel branch calls bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... await getCalendar(credential) ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) }). This PR adds an await ahead of the loop, so every push happens later. The handler snapshots apiDeletes at line 652 (prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) and awaits only that copy, so these deletions are neither awaited nor reflected in the response. Cancellation can return success before calendar events are removed, and any rejection is an unhandled rejection. Use for...of with await and push into apiDeletes before the final Promise.all.

import() calls are evaluated eagerly, so the modules are not actually deferred

Each entry is written as a direct import("./x") call inside the object literal. Those calls run when index.ts is evaluated, so every app module still starts loading on the first import of @calcom/app-store, just without blocking. The only change is that the module evaluation no longer blocks synchronously. If the goal is lazy loading, each entry should be a function such as () => import("./x") that consumers invoke only when needed. As written, the PR does not reduce load work or startup cost.

getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited getCalendar promises in a sync function

getCalendarCredentials is still synchronous, but getCalendar is now async, so the calendar field of each returned entry is a Promise<Calendar | null>. Only getConnectedCalendars awaits it (line 48). Any other consumer that uses the field as a Calendar will fail to typecheck, and any rejection from getCalendar (for example a CalendarService constructor throw) in an entry that is never awaited becomes an unhandled rejection. The return type should make the Promise explicit, or the function should become async and its callers should await it.

Sync-to-async signature changes have no test updates

getCalendar changes from a synchronous return to Promise<Calendar | null>, and deleteMeeting, deleteEvent, getVideoAdapters and about 12 call sites across 10 files gain awaits. The PR touches no test files. Existing unit tests that stub getCalendar, deleteMeeting or appStore synchronously will break or silently pass against the wrong shape. The unhandled-rejection problems in the forEach call sites would also go undetected because no test exercises the failure paths of these functions.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
